patches.reason: The board setup writes `map` from position 1 on and sets `map[0]=0` only afterwards, and the end squares at `map[nmap+i]`, so Groovy's list grew with a null at position 0 until then; the list is therefore typed as holding null, and every later `map[i]` read needs a null test that the moves never make (22 compile errors). `map` is empty when the setup starts, the shuffled blocks hold exactly `nblock` squares each and `imap` ends at `nmap`, so setting `map[0]` first and appending each square in turn builds the same list; a Groovy run gives identical maps for every board size from 30 to 2000.
